paper_sections.title: Binge Eating (BE) and Obesity: Brain Activity and Psychological Measures before and after Roux-En-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB)
Change in Activation from Baseline to 4 Months Post (T1 > T2)

description.value: The study examined brain activity and psychological measures related to binge eating and food cues before and four months after bariatric surgery, comparing women undergoing RYGB with BMI-matched women who did not undergo treatment.

design.value: Prospective longitudinal study of healthy Class III women with obesity, including 15 participants who opted for RYGB surgery and 13 BMI-matched women who did not undergo treatment. Participants underwent fMRI approximately 1 month before and 4 months after surgery, or at matched intervals for the NT group; participants were classified by binge-eating status as BE or NB.

name.value: Questionnaire of Eating and Weight Patterns Revised (QEWP-R)

description.value: Used to assess binge-eating status.
Used at baseline in assessment according to DSM-5 and classification of binge-eating status.
Assesses emotional eating in response to positive and negative emotions and situations; mean scores are calculated for positive and negative emotions and situations.

Assesses the impact of food-abundant environments, including appetite-related thoughts, feelings, motivations, food liking, and appetitive drive at three levels of food proximity: food available, food present, and food tasted.
Used at four months to reassess binge-eating status; includes modified questions pertaining to bariatric surgery in place of the EDE-Q.
Used with a Tanita scale to measure body fat.

source_definition.value: Participants who endorsed overeating with loss of control and either met full criteria or subthreshold criteria for binge eating.
Participants who did not meet either full criteria or sub-threshold criteria for BE.
baseline BMI entered as a covariate or nuisance covariate.
The baseline score entered as a covariate for the 4-month outcome psychological measures.

description.value: Women with obesity who opted for Roux-En-Y gastric bypass surgery.

inclusion_criteria.value: severe obesity (BMI = 40–50 kg/m2), 18–65 years old, candidacy for RYGB, relatively good health

exclusion_criteria.value: 10% weight fluctuation in the previous three months; pregnancy, lactation, planning to become pregnant in next 18 months, or <1 year postpartum; smoking cessation in the previous three months or smoking more than five cigarettes per week; known claustrophobia for an fMRI enclosure; metal implants, non-removable metallic dental retainers, or pacemakers; consumption of four or more alcoholic drinks per day; recreational drug use in the previous six months; history of anorexia nervosa; history of hospitalization for a psychiatric condition; history of alcohol or drug dependence; previous bariatric surgery

recruitment_method.value: recruited from patients at Mount Sinai Morningside Hospital in New York City

medical_condition.value: healthy Class III (BMI > 40 kg/m2) women with obesity

clinical_characteristics.value: Participants underwent RYGB; one participant had actually undergone sleeve gastrectomy but was retained in the analysis.

task_description.value: Participants viewed high-energy-food, low-energy-food, and non-food visual stimuli in six runs. Each run contained 10 stimuli of the same type, presented for four seconds each, with pre- and post-stimulus crosshair baselines.

stimuli.value: HEF stimuli included cakes, ice cream, and fast foods; LEF stimuli consisted of fruits and vegetables; NF stimuli consisted of basic office supplies, such as tape, staplers, and rubber bands.

instrument.value: 1.5 GE Tesla twin-speed scanner with supine quadrature RF head coil

description.value: Functional T2*-weighted images with a gradient echo pulse sequence were obtained. Scans were conducted in the morning between 9–11 am. During each run, 36 whole-brain scans were taken, each consisting of 25 contiguous slices, 4 mm thick, parallel to the AC/PC line, with a 19 × 19 cm2 view, 128 × 128 matrix size, and 1.5 × 1.5 mm2 in-plane resolution.

Prior to statistical analyses, the realigned T2*-weighted volumes were slice-time corrected, spatially transformed to a standardized brain (Montreal Neurologic Institute), and smoothed with an 8-mm full-width half-maximum Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: spatial transformation to a standardized Montreal Neurologic Institute brain
smoothing with an 8-mm full-width half-maximum Gaussian kernel
discarding the first three scans of each run to attain magnetic equilibration

model_settings.value: First-level regressors were created by convolving the onset of each condition with the canonical HRF with duration of 40 s. Contrasts included Food > NF and HEF > LEF at baseline, 4 months post, and T1 > T2.

model_type.value: group random effects (2nd-level) multiple regression analyses

model_settings.value: Predictor variables were experimental group (BE vs. NB; RYGB vs. NT) and BMI as a nuisance covariate. Main comparisons included overall effects of experimental group at baseline, 4 months post-surgery, and baseline > post contrasts, as well as two-way interactions between experimental and intervention groups.
One thousand bootstrap samples were performed using a bias corrected and accelerated confidence interval.

estimator.value: bias corrected and accelerated bootstrap confidence interval

roi_definition.value: 10 mm spheres around MNI coordinates that we previously reported for nine ROIs

definition.value: Food > Non-Food (NF), BE > NB at baseline (Timepoint 1, T1)

multiple_comparison_method.value: false discovery rate (FDR) across all tests conducted; a less stringent exploratory threshold of p < 0.006 uncorrected

correction_scope.value: across all tests conducted, 19 contrasts × 9 ROIs

model_representation_notes.value: Test statistics were reported for the original unsampled data, but degrees of freedom were not reported because p-values were estimated using nonparametric bootstrapping with 1,000 bootstrap samples.

interpretations.value: There was greater precuneus brain activity in the BE group compared with the NB group in response to Food vs. NF cues at baseline (t = 2.74, p = 0.003 uncorrected, p = 0.12 corrected). Precuneus activation in BE participants in response to NF was both lower and negative relative to the crosshairs control.

definition.value: Food > Non-Food (NF), BE > NB at 4 months post-surgery (Timepoint 2, T2)

interpretations.value: At 4 months post-surgery, there was greater brain activity in the thalamus in the BE group in response to Food vs. NF cues, whereas the NB group showed greater thalamus activity in response to NF vs. Food cues (t = 3.89, p = 0.00007 uncorrected, p = 0.014 corrected). There was also greater precuneus brain activity in the BE group compared with the NB group in response to Food vs. NF cues (t = 2.76, p = 0.003 uncorrected).

definition.value: At 4 months post-surgery (T2): HEF > LEF, NT > RYGB, BE > NB

interpretations.value: There was an interaction between treatment and experimental group for brain activity in the middle occipital gyrus (t = 3.06, p = 0.0012 uncorrected). RYGB BE participants had the lowest middle occipital gyrus brain activity in response to HEF, while RYGB NB participants had the highest brain activity in response to HEF cues. There was also an interaction between treatment and experimental group in the inferior frontal gyrus (t = 3.09, p = 0.003 uncorrected); the RYGB NB group had the highest inferior frontal gyrus brain activity in response to HEF cues and the NT NB group had the lowest.
